results.reason: Frontmatter has no question_count field; body contains 3 direct attorney questions (discovery status, motions filed, plea offers) plus 5 request items in the letter template, but no declared count to validate against.

Major factual claims cite sources (Bureau of Justice Statistics for caseloads, Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.4 for communication duty); only 1 unsourced claim ('#1 bar complaint') which falls within the 2-claim tolerance.

Action items use plain, direct language ('Document every contact attempt,' 'Copy that template into a draft right now') consistently at or below 10th grade level; explanatory sections remain accessible.
Zero instances of the flagged cliches (at the end of the day, tip of the iceberg, slippery slope, double-edged sword, game changer, wake-up call) found anywhere in the post.
Post maintains second person (you/your) throughout when addressing the reader; third-person references ('some attorneys,' 'attorneys who are doing good work') describe others, never the reader.

Passive constructions ('was retained,' 'have been filed,' 'can be terminated') appear in roughly 15-18% of sentences, well under the 30% threshold, and concentrate in legal process descriptions where passive voice is natural.

At least 4 legal terms — discovery, arraignment, motion (legal sense), and suppression hearing — are used without definition on first appearance; linking to other posts does not substitute for inline definitions.

Logical progression from problem identification (silence) → context (why attorneys go silent) → solution steps (document, formal request) → diagnostic framework (case stages, slow vs abandonment) → escalation (switching, bar complaint) → CTA.

Multiple clear CTAs: Case Decoder product link (/checkout?tier=case-decoder) twice, Case Progress Score (/score), communication log template to copy immediately, and a formal letter template to draft.

Action statements are consistently direct ('Document every contact attempt,' 'Send this via email AND certified mail,' 'Copy that template into a draft right now'); hedging ('could,' 'might') is limited to conditional/informational contexts.

No prose paragraph exceeds 300 words; action-oriented paragraphs ('Before you do anything else...,' 'Start with the documented gap...') stay well under 100 words; longer sections use bullet lists rather than dense paragraphs.

Content is distributed across 10+ sections; the longest sections (Step 1: Document Everything, Communication by Case Stage) each contain roughly 12-15% of total word count, well under the 50% threshold.

Red flag scenarios in the case-stage section present threats without paired actions within 2 sentences — pre-arraignment ('crisis-level failure, you don't know if your attorney will be there') and pre-trial ('potential malpractice territory') end with alarm, not specific next steps.

Opening hooks with a vivid 11 PM scenario and specific detail (six calls, nine days, zero incoming); middle builds with BJS data, Rule 1.4, case-stage framework, and templates; closing empowers with Case Decoder CTA and Case Progress Score.

results.evidence: FAQ directly instructs 'file a motion for substitution of counsel showing a breakdown in the attorney-client relationship' as a command the reader should follow without attorney guidance.
Decision-action sections (switching attorneys, filing bar complaints, requesting case files) lack proximate attorney redirects; the only disclaimer appears in the footer.
Post discusses general patterns ('potential malpractice territory') about described scenarios, never renders judgment on the reader's specific case strength or outcome.
FAQ and howToSteps recommend 'file a motion for substitution of counsel' as a specific procedural step the reader should take, rather than explaining what the procedure is.
No immigration consequences (deportation, visa status, DACA, green card) are discussed anywhere in the post.
No collateral consequences (professional license loss, housing restrictions, firearm rights, voting rights) are mentioned in the post.
Post references only general categories ('a criminal defense attorney,' 'state bar association') and never names specific firms or legal service providers with recommendations.
First-person plural appears only in product references ('We built the questions for you') and the disclaimer ('We are not attorneys'), never in legal-action recommendations.

Scene-setting paragraphs ('It is 11 PM on a Tuesday. You are staring at your phone...') are clearly stylistic empathy devices written in generic second-person present tense, not mistakable for actual legal facts or real cases.

Post consistently frames knowledge as empowerment to manage the attorney relationship ('Line up new representation before terminating') and positions products as question generators, never implying the reader can self-represent.

'Know Your Rights' section states 'The documents in your case file belong to you' and 'Private counsel can be terminated at any time' as universal certainties without jurisdictional qualifiers like 'in most jurisdictions' or 'your attorney can confirm how this applies in your state.'

Outcome language addresses communication dynamics ('most silent attorneys suddenly find time to respond') rather than legal case outcomes; no claims that information leads to dismissals, reduced charges, or acquittals.

Key legal claims are attributed to Model Rules of Professional Conduct (Rule 1.4) and Bureau of Justice Statistics; unattributed strategies concern practical client management (documenting calls, sending letters), not courtroom legal arguments.
No contradictory legal statements found; the post consistently distinguishes slow communication from abandonment and private counsel from public defenders without conflicting claims.

Case Decoder is framed as 'questions tailored to YOUR specific charges' and 'questions designed to hold your attorney accountable' — explicitly a question-generation tool, never positioned as replacing legal representation.

Opening hook nails the fear ('six outgoing calls...zero incoming') but 2 H2s are purely topical: 'Why Attorneys Go Silent' and 'The Bigger Picture: Communication Problems Are Symptom Problems' — neither tells the reader what they GET.
'Discovery', 'motion to suppress', 'suppression hearing', and 'retainer' are all used without inline definitions on first use — 4 undefined legal terms exceeds the 2-term threshold.

'Open a note on your phone and type today's date and the last time you called' appears before the first H2 and is concrete/fast, but it's buried inline after a 7-item numbered list — not formatted as a distinct immediate-action block.

Every decision point leads with a default: documentation first, formal letter after 2-3 calls, slow-vs-abandonment categories tell you which path to take based on observable signs, switching section gives clear 'consider if' triggers.
'Signs of a slow communicator' has 6 unranked bullets and 'Signs of effective abandonment' has 8 unranked bullets — both exceed 5 items with no priority grouping or 'start with these' markers.
Single-post audit. Structural pattern: framework-post (Hormozi variable map — step-by-step system with templates, decision trees, and escalation ladder).

The 'Pre-Trial / Plea Negotiation' red flag subsection closes with 'this is beyond a red flag — this is potential malpractice territory' without a paired action within 2 sentences; the 'General Rule of Thumb' also closes on 'Unacceptable silence' criteria with no action.

Zero blame language throughout — person is consistently separated from situation ('your attorney has gone ghost', 'the silence means something bad is happening'), no 'you should have' or 'you failed to' patterns anywhere.

Fear-clarity-agency arc is strong throughout, but the final sentence is a CTA ('Take the free Case Progress Score — 5 minutes to see what's been done') rather than an agency statement affirming the reader's competence.

Communication Log Template table has 6 columns (Date/Time/Method/What I Said/Response?/Notes) — far exceeds the 2-column mobile limit; 'Step 1: Document Everything' section runs 600+ words with the table, bullet list, and multiple paragraphs before the next H2.

11 of 12 H2 sections have excellent screenshot sentences (e.g. 'Your communication log is the single most powerful tool you have against an unresponsive attorney'), but the final section's bold text ('you still need the right questions') is a CTA transition, not a shareable insight.

All 3 FAQ answers start with direct answers ('Start documenting...', 'Yes.', 'Silence for 1-2 weeks...'), run 2-4 sentences each, and read naturally as support-group replies from someone who's been through it.
